data.content_ref: inline:The target's scope is artificially narrowed to complex, emergent-outcome tasks, but it presents its claim as a general verdict on the comparative reliability of experts vs checklist panels. The problem asks which is more reliable 'on average' across tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes. By excluding discrete/algorithmic tasks (listed as a countercondition) — which are a large share of verifiable-outcome tasks and exactly where checklists excel — the target sidesteps the averaged comparison the problem actually demands. Its mechanism (holistic synthesis vs additive reliability) is then argument for a subset, not an answer to the average-over-all-verifiable-tasks claim.
